*Reasoning as the farmer:*

Aiya, I been farming this land 40 years. At 65, just me and my wife at home now — kids went to work in town. 9.5 mu isn't big, but it's enough to keep us busy. I split it like always: about 6.5 mu for wheat-maize rotation, and 3 mu for cotton on the lower field. Used to do more cotton when the kids were here to help pick, but now my back can't take it, and we already hire a couple neighbors for the picking time.

For wheat I do what I always do — plant in October, two bags of compound (15-15-15) at sowing, that's about 50 jin per mu. Then when it joints in spring, one bag of urea per mu, maybe a little more if it looks pale. My neighbor old Wang put on less last year and his yield dropped, so I won't cut back. Water it three or four times — once before winter, once at jointing, once at heading, and one more if May is dry. Well water costs money to pump, so I don't waste it.

Maize goes in right after wheat harvest in June, no time to waste — maybe two days to clear stubble and direct-seed with the small planter we share with my brother-in-law. Use the Zhengdan hybrid, everyone around here uses it. One bag compound at planting, urea topdress when it's knee-high. Maize doesn't need much water if July rains come, maybe one or two irrigations.

Cotton I plant late April. Use the local Bt variety, doesn't need much spraying for bollworm. Three pickings starting September. Cotton price has been so-so — last year I got about 6 yuan per jin. If price drops more next year, maybe I'll cut cotton and rest the land or rent it out.
